title: A finite morphism with closed-immersive fibre is closed-immersive nearby
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and let $s\in S$. Write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-weil-residue-field]. If $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then there exists an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Lemma 04DG proof, Nakayama and spreading-out sentences (lines 734-743)

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood Spec A of s, with corresponding prime p. Its inverse image under the finite morphism is Spec B, with B a finite A-module. The affine fibre-product and residue-field identifications identify the fibre map with Spec of κ(p) → κ(p) ⊗[A] B. Since this is a closed immersion, the ring map is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 04DG proof, Nakayama and spreading-out sentences (lines 734-743)

proof.text: Let N be the A-submodule image of A → B and Q = B/N, a finite A-module. Right exactness of tensor product shows κ(p) ⊗[A] Q = 0. After localizing at p this is the quotient of Q_p by the maximal ideal of A_p times Q_p. Nakayama gives Q_p = 0. Equivalently, A_p → B_p is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 04DG proof, Nakayama and spreading-out sentences (lines 734-743)

proof.text: The support of the finite module Q is the zero locus of its annihilator. As Q_p = 0, choose a in Ann(Q) outside p. Then Q_a = 0 and right exactness of localization makes A_a → B_a surjective.

source.place: Lemma 04DG proof, Nakayama and spreading-out sentences (lines 734-743)

proof.text: The principal open U = D(a) contains s. The principal-localization open immersions identify f restricted over U with Spec(B_a) → Spec(A_a). The surjective ring map A_a → B_a makes this a closed immersion. Composing U with the original affine neighbourhood inclusion produces the required open of S. The empty fibre is allowed: its zero ring gives the same vanishing of κ(p) ⊗ Q.

For a finite morphism of schemes, a closed immersion of the fibre extends to a closed immersion on a neighbourhood
